en.title: Fewest Machines Preserving the Sum of Adjacent Absolute Differences
en.description:
You may delete some elements from the array; the remaining elements keep their relative order and at least 1 must remain. The sum of absolute differences between adjacent elements of the remaining array must equal that of the original array. Find the minimum number of elements kept (not the number deleted).

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains the array. 1≤n≤200000, elements 0..10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: keep 1, 2, 1; the sum of adjacent differences is still 2, and at least 3 elements are needed. Example 2: the sum is 0, so keeping any 1 element is enough. Example 3: keep only 1 and 4; the total difference 3 is unchanged, so the answer is 2.
hints: Collapse runs of equal consecutive values. If only one value remains the answer is 1; otherwise keep the first and last elements plus every turning point where the sequence switches between strictly increasing and strictly decreasing.
